issues.legal_issue: A writ challenge to an administrative rejection may be denied for unexplained and unjustified delay.
material_facts: The applicant’s request for a quarry lease was rejected after the governing relaxation rule had been repealed.
The applicant did not challenge the rejection for several years and gave no justifiable reason for waiting.
After the delayed writ petition was filed, an interim order permitted quarrying, and a third party complained that the applicant was interfering with an area leased to that party.
issues.conclusion: The writ petition was hopelessly belated and was rightly dismissed for laches; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Whether delay bars relief depends on the facts of each case; there is no hard-and-fast rule. Delay does not invariably defeat a claim, particularly where the respondent’s position has not been irretrievably altered or undue hardship caused, but an unexplained and unjustified prolonged delay may warrant denying writ relief. The Court considered P.C. Sethi v. Union of India, K. Thimmappa v. Chairman, Central Board of Directors, State Bank of India, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd. v. Dolly Das, Dehri Rohtas Light Railway Company Ltd. v. District Board, Bhojpur, and State of Orissa v. Lochan Nayak.

predicates.writ_challenge_to_administrative_rejecti: A person sought writ relief challenging an administrative decision that rejected the person’s application.
predicates.substantial_unexplained_delay: The person waited a substantial period after the rejection before seeking writ relief and did not explain the delay.
predicates.no_justification_for_waiting: The person had no justifiable reason for waiting to challenge the rejection.
predicates.writ_relief_denied_for_laches: The court denies writ relief because the challenge was brought after substantial, unjustified delay.

issues.definition: When a person brings a writ challenge to an administrative rejection only after substantial unexplained delay and has no justification for waiting, the court may deny writ relief for laches.

issues.legal_issue: A pending application for a discretionary mining lease is governed by the rules in force when the application is disposed of, and a prior order directing consideration does not preserve a right to grant under a repealed rule.
material_facts: The applicant sought a quarry lease under a rule that empowered the government to grant or renew leases in special cases.
A court had directed the government to consider and dispose of the application, but had not adjudicated an entitlement to a lease.
The rule was repealed before the government disposed of the application, which it then rejected.
The applicant claimed that the application should be considered under the rule as it stood when the application was made.
issues.conclusion: The repeal removed the basis for granting the application under the former rule; the applicant had no vested right to a mining lease, and the authority could not grant the lease under that repealed rule.
issues.legal_principle: Under Rule 39 of the Tamil Nadu Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 1959, the State Government had power to grant or renew a lease or permission in special cases. No one has a vested right to the grant or renewal of a mining lease, or to have an application decided under the rules in force when it was made. A pending application is dealt with under the rules in force on the date of disposal. The Court relied on State of Tamil Nadu v. M/s. Hind Stone, (1981) 2 SCC 205, and P.T.R. Exports (Madras) Pvt. Ltd. v. Union of India, (1996) 5 SCC 268. It distinguished decisions concerning changes to the basis of rights already decided, because the earlier order here required only consideration of the application and had not established a right to a lease.

predicates.discretionary_mining_lease_application_p: An applicant had a pending request for a mining lease that could be granted in special cases.
predicates.prior_order_only_required_consideration: A court had directed the authority to consider the application but had not decided that the applicant was entitled to a lease.
predicates.governing_rule_repealed_before_disposal: The rule under which the application was made was repealed before the authority disposed of it.
predicates.application_governed_by_rules_at_disposa: The authority must decide the pending application under the rules in force when it disposes of the application.

issues.definition: If a discretionary mining lease application remains pending after a court has ordered only that it be considered, and the governing rule is repealed before disposal, the application is governed by the rules in force at disposal.
